body:
**Note (adr): Prompt points at docs/adr/, which does not exist here**

The prompt tells Claude that "the ADRs in docs/adr/ hold its decisions", but this repository keeps them in `apps/documentation/src/content/docs/architecture/decisions/`. `docs/adr/` is a path from the kit's original repository. Claude will find nothing there, so it can't check changes against accepted decisions, and the "contradicts an accepted decision" rule in RULES won't work. Make the ADR directory configurable, or point the prompt at the real path. `.github/claude-review.md` could name it.

**Note (security): Unpinned installer piped to bash in a job that holds the API key**

`curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash -s "$CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION"` pins the Claude Code version but not the installer script. The installer is fetched live and run in the same job that later receives `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. The same step appears in `on-demand` at line 158. Consider verifying a checksum of the installer or the binary, or installing from a pinned npm package. The workflow also uses floating action tags (`actions/checkout@v4`, `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`). If that matches the other workflows here, ignore this.

**Note (security): The `review` job runs the PR head's own script with the API key**

In `review`, the checkout is the PR head and the script runs from that checkout. A same-repo PR that edits `scripts/claude-review.ts`, `.claude/` or `bunfig.toml` can exfiltrate `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or alter the budget. The header and ADR 0028 accept this under the owner-only trust assumption. The `on-demand` job already runs the default branch's script, so `review` could do the same by checking out the default branch's `scripts/` the way `on-demand` does. That would remove the inconsistency cheaply. The ADR's "What would reopen this" already covers a second collaborator joining.

**Note (correctness): `cancel-in-progress` on on-demand lets any later @claude comment kill a running review**

The group is per PR with `cancel-in-progress: true`. If the owner comments `@claude review`, then a quick `@claude why …` question before it finishes, the review is cancelled after Claude has already spent budget. Nothing is posted and the next run starts over. Because the cancelled run never posts a marker, nothing is corrupted, but the spend is wasted. Consider `cancel-in-progress: false` so runs queue.

Fixed in 24527c8: the script reads `CLAUDE_REVIEW_ADR_DIR` (default `docs/adr`, so the kit still works elsewhere) and the workflow sets it to `apps/documentation/src/content/docs/architecture/decisions`. A test covers both cases.

Fixed in f4045c0: both jobs now download the 2.1.304 linux-x64 binary directly and check it with `sha256sum -c` against `CLAUDE_CODE_SHA256`, taken from the release manifest (verified locally against the downloaded file). install.sh is no longer fetched. The floating action tags match every other workflow here, so they stay.

Keeping the head script here, and 988972b adds a comment explaining why. On `pull_request` the workflow file itself comes from the PR head, so a branch that can edit `scripts/claude-review.ts` can also edit this job to check out whatever it wants. Checking out the default branch's script would look like protection without being one. `on-demand` is different because `issue_comment` runs the default branch's workflow. The owner-only trust assumption in ADR 0028 is what covers this job.

Fixed in 780f6c8: `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a follow-up `@claude` comment queues behind a running review. GitHub keeps only one pending run per group, so in a burst of three comments the middle one is dropped; the comment in the workflow says so.
